solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A theme of allergic hypersensitivity

parts.note: a theme is the subject or topic of a talk or essay

explanation.surface: A medical writer's chosen subject: the topic of allergic hypersensitivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Atopic is the medical adjective for an inherited tendency to allergies such as eczema and hay fever.

clue.text: Crown of Irish hill contains one

indicators.note: contains says the hill's name holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: the Hill of Tara in County Meath was the seat of the ancient High Kings of Ireland
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The crown of an Irish hill holds a single something.
explanation.walkthrough: Tara is fitting: it was where Irish kings were crowned.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headdress, a kind of small crown worn by royalty or a bride.

clue.text: Mobile phone company: one from 23 supported by a country in Asia once

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supported by another sits above it, so the A comes last
mobile means able to move about, so the letters of phone move into a new order

parts.note: the chemical company named in the clue to 23 across is ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries

explanation.surface: A mobile phone firm described as sitting beneath a former Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: PHOEN is the shuffle of PHONE; ICI is the company from 23 across, and A goes at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was an ancient maritime civilisation on the coast of the Levant, now Lebanon and Syria, so a land of Asia in former times.

clue.text: Actor's upset his fellow actor?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or thrown into disorder, so the letters of the clue word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor is put out by the person sharing the stage with him.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is part of the anagram fodder, giving the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star shares top billing with another performer, so is that actor's colleague on screen or stage.

clue.text: Drummer at bash for Apollo launch?

parts.note: Keith Moon was the drummer of The Who
to have a bash at something is to have a shot at it, an attempt

explanation.surface: A drummer at a party looks forward to a space launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' looks like a party; here it is an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonshot is a launch of a spacecraft to the Moon, as the Apollo missions were; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Riverside club with a line in freshly crumbed dogfish

indicators.note: in puts the line inside the rearranged letters
freshly suggests the words are made anew, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A riverside eatery serves fish in fresh breadcrumbs, lined up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riverside Stadium is Middlesbrough Football Club's ground in the north-east of England, on the River Tees.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlesbrough FC play at the Riverside Stadium, so the club can be named by its home ground.

clue.text: Where fruit grows in bottom of gully below mountains in Oregon

indicators.note: in a down entry, below means the next piece comes underneath, at the end
in says the mountains sit inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: OR is the postal abbreviation for Oregon
a range is a chain of mountains

indicators.note: bottom of a down word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A description of a fruit-growing spot at the foot of a gully in Oregon's mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glasshouse built for growing citrus trees in cooler climates.

clue.text: Dry, therefore, by end of autumn's months

parts.note: so and therefore both mean 'for that reason'
September, October and November all finish with the same three letters

explanation.surface: A dry spell, apparently, through the end of the autumn months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' suggests weather; here it means not drinking alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dry has given up alcohol, so is not drunk: a teetotal sense of the word.

clue.text: Father of unexpectedly great no.11

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so the letters turn up in a new order

parts.note: no. stays as the letters NO, and 11 is written as II, two Roman ones

explanation.surface: A surprising entry about a fine number eleven player's father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in fathering an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To father something is to bring it into being, to start or create it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Louts say nothing when involved with house break-in

indicators.note: break-in says the next piece breaks into the jumbled letters
involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Thugs keep silent when caught up in a burglary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SAY as YAS, and 'break-in' puts the house and the nothing inside it. 'break-in' poses as a burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: Yahoos are coarse, boorish people, after the brutish humans in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Stupid idea: 50% rum-based liqueur

indicators.note: a stupid idea is a muddled one, so its letters get muddled too
50% takes the first half of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A foolish notion: a liqueur half made of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' takes RUMB, half of 'rum-based'; 'Stupid' shuffles it with IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Drambuie is a Scotch whisky liqueur flavoured with honey and herbs.

clue.text: Water dropping in river with own Scottish season

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
ain is the Scots word for own
fall is the American name for autumn

explanation.surface: A Scottish river getting its own season of wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall is water falling from the sky as precipitation, a descriptive phrase for it.

clue.text: Neil rightly backed contents displaying nude women?

indicators.note: backed says the hidden letters are read backwards
contents points to letters held inside the words Neil rightly

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Neil correctly supported a magazine's content of naked women.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'contents' into the definition; it is the signal for letters held inside the words, leaving 'displaying nude women' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A girlie magazine or show is one featuring pictures of scantily clad or naked women.

clue.text: Great online photo

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in email
pic is short for picture or photograph

explanation.surface: Praise for a picture posted on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is slang for impressive or excellent, as well as grand in scale.

clue.text: Writer from the French left, initially offended by American hanging

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
du means of the or from the in French

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: US stands for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: A French-speaking writer, offended, quits and leaves an American hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendulous means drooping or dangling loosely, as things that hang down do.

clue.text: Small luminous discharge round old woman's tumours

parts.note: an arc is a glowing electrical discharge between electrodes
O is round in shape
an old woman is slang for one's mother, ma, here possessive

explanation.surface: A small glowing discharge surrounds an elderly woman's growths.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcomas are malignant growths arising in connective tissue such as bone or muscle.

clue.text: Standard ordnance content's replaced by sawn-off rifle and ammo

indicators.note: says the inside of the word ordnance is swapped out for what follows, keeping its outer letters
sawn-off means shortened at the end, so each of rifle and ammo loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A standard-issue weapons inventory, swapped for a sawn-off rifle and ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content's replaced by' keeps O and E of 'ordnance'; 'sawn-off' trims RIFLE and AMMO to RIFL and AMM.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the scarlet banner of the early kings of France, a battle standard or flag.

clue.text: Violinist without upright character is harder to handle

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the violinist goes around the letter

parts.note: a fiddler plays the fiddle, an informal name for the violin
the capital I is a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: A violinist lacking integrity is a trickier proposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddly means awkward and needing delicate handling, so the comparative means more awkward to manage.

clue.text: New Nikes are more slippery

indicators.note: new means made over, so the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Fresh trainers are less grippy underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Nike is a sportswear brand; the answer echoes 'sneakers' too.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery can mean shifty and untrustworthy, and sneaky people are sly and evasive in the same way.

clue.text: Composer of five symphonies

indicators.note: of signals letters taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A composer credited with five symphonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer known for his symphonies and The Unanswered Question.

clue.text: Get in and bat, getting out at end of over

indicators.note: at end of says the rearranged letters come after the abbreviation for over

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: getting out suggests disarray, so the letters of in and bat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction: get in and bat, then get out when the over ends.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain is to get or acquire something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Offer more than I do, but get beaten

indicators.note: to get beaten is to be knocked about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A rival at an auction offers more than I do, but still loses.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbid is to bid higher than a rival, offering a larger sum at auction.

clue.text: Swell cure for disease in livestock

definitions.meaning: to swell up or puff out with gas or fluid
to cure herring partly by smoking
a condition of cattle and sheep in which gas distends the stomach

explanation.surface: Splendid news: a remedy for an illness affecting farm animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' poses as the slang adjective for great; 'cure' as a remedy. A bloater is a cured herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloat means puff up, cure fish by smoking, and a gassy stomach ailment of ruminants.

clue.text: Liberal character returned, heading up chemical company in depressed areas

indicators.note: heading up says the reversed pieces lead the next one
returned says these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries

explanation.surface: A Liberal comes back to lead a chemical firm in deprived regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LIBMU into UMBIL. 'depressed areas' poses as economic decline; navels are hollows.
explanation.definitionFit: The navels are hollows in the belly, so plural depressions in the body's surface.

clue.text: Italian painter's half-completed Venetian scene?

indicators.note: half-completed means only part of the name is kept, the front portion

parts.note: Canaletto was the eighteenth-century Venetian painter of city views

explanation.surface: An Italian artist's unfinished view of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-completed' drops ETTO from CANALETTO, leaving roughly the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterways are the defining sight of Venice and the subject of many of Canaletto's paintings.

clue.text: Light aircraft carrying lion crashed into stone pillar

indicators.note: carrying says the aircraft holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: the de Havilland Moth was a famous British light aircraft

indicators.note: crashed means wrecked, so the letters of lion are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A small plane with a lion on board crashes into a stone column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' looks like the plane's fate but scrambles the lion; 'carrying' puts that inside the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A monolith is a single great block of stone standing upright, like a standing stone or obelisk.

clue.text: Tree old man cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated means worked or tilled, so the letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly gardener grows a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is a tree of the rose family grown for its edible nuts.

clue.text: Hidden books man found on tablets

indicators.note: found on says the books and man come after the tablets

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so ES for tablets
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: Secret books of a man discovered on stone tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is obscure, understood only by a select inner circle, so concealed from most.

clue.text: Bug River flows back, replacing current in much longer river

indicators.note: replacing says one piece takes the place of another inside the long river

parts.note: the Nile is far longer than the Dee
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: flows back says the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales

explanation.surface: A river reverses, displacing the flow of a far longer one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flows back' turns DEE into EED, which takes the place of I in NILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or annoy them, as to bug someone is.
